To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) clathrin (and its AP-1 complex) is involved in the apical transport of proteins and sphingolipids during lumen formation in the C. elegans intestine; (2) this transport pathway is distinct from the basolateral clathrin-dependent endocytosis route, as it does not require the dynamin-1 ortholog dyn-1; and (3) clathrin/AP1 and sphingolips are required for
clathrin and its AP- 1 adaptor regulate apical polarity during C. elegas tubulogenesis.
clathrin coats vesicular traffic on an apical transport route and that this route converges with a sphingomyelin-dependent pathway to establish apical membrane polarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of epithelial cell polarity and tubulogenesis.
the molecular mechanisms of tubulogenesis, a key step in organ formation.
a previously unknown clathrin/AP1-dependent apical transport path and its role during lumen morphogenesis in the C elegans intestine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clathrin/AP1 is involved in apical transport in C. elegans and that this is a novel function for clathrin/AP complexes.
clathrin/AP1-mediated vesicular transport is involved in apical membrane polarity during tubulogenesis in C. elegans.
the CHC-1/Adaptor complex 1 (AP-1) complex is a key component of a trafficking pathway that mediates apical polarity and de novo lumen formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
clathrin/AP1-mediated polarized trafficking is a novel and conserved process for establishing apical membrane identity and that it functions to generate lumenal domains in the C.  elegans intestine.
clathrin and AP1 have a previously unappreciated function in polarizing apical membrane domains during lumen formation in C. elegans.
clathrin and AP1 are involved in apical polarity and lumens morphogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CHC-1-mediated trafficking path is not limited to basolaterally directed transport.
the clathrin machinery can function in apical membrane polarity during lumen formation, and that it can intersect with other trafficking pathways.
clathrin-mediated trafficking can play a role in apical polarity and tubulogenesis, which is not limited to the basolateral route.
